bug_description.normalized: The harness passes the attacker-controlled bytes into `hb_blob_create()`, which stores them in an `hb_blob_t` backing the face/font used by the first fixed UTF-8 `hb_shape()` call. Adding that string grows the buffer's `info` array and leaves spare capacity uninitialized. Feature collection always adds horizontal `kern` with `F_HAS_FALLBACK`, so `hb_ot_shape_planner_t::compile()` materializes a non-zero planner-global `kern_mask` and sets `plan.has_kern` even without font-provided kerning data. Because the same face lacks GPOS, `hb_ot_shape_internal()` enables fallback positioning. During GSUB, the generic forward lookup walk finishes with `buffer->idx == buffer->len`; `hb_ot_position()` then calls `clear_positions()`, which zeroes positions but preserves that stale cursor. `_hb_ot_shape_fallback_kern()` iterates with local `idx`, but its guard reads `buffer->cur().mask`, i.e. `info[buffer->idx].mask`, so the witnessed run consumes the uninitialized first tail slot just past the initialized glyph range. The fix changes the read to `info[idx].mask`.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that consumes attacker-controlled input. It stores the fuzzer-supplied byte pointer into library state, which later backs all font-table reads through the face and font on the crashing path.
source.value_from: Raw fuzzer bytes `data[0..size-1]` passed from the PoC into `hb_blob_create()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MSan crash site. The fallback-kern guard reads `info[buffer->idx].mask` through `buffer->cur()` instead of `info[idx].mask`; with the preserved stale cursor at `buffer->len`, this tests the first uninitialized tail slot in the `info` allocation.

root_cause.description: The loop is indexed by local `idx`, but the guard dereferences `buffer->cur()`, which uses the persistent buffer cursor instead of the loop index. Because GSUB left `buffer->idx == buffer->len` and `clear_positions()` did not reset it, the guard reads `info[len].mask` from uninitialized tail storage. The patch fixes this by reading `info[idx].mask`.

parser_admitted.description: The witness enters the first `hb_shape(font, buffer, NULL, 0)` call on the fixed UTF-8 buffer. Both the crash stack and the MSan heap-origin stack belong to this call, not to the later UTF-32 shaping branch.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSan reports the uninitialized value as created by this heap allocation while growing the fixed-text buffer's glyph-info array. The unused tail of the new `info` allocation remains indeterminate until later writes initialize specific elements.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The first fixed-text `hb_buffer_add_utf8` call triggers `ensure()` and `enlarge()` on the glyph-info array before the crashing `hb_shape()` invocation.
tainted_value_origin.note: The sanitizer origin stack names `hb_buffer_t::enlarge` at line 138 and traces it back through `hb_buffer_add_utf<hb_utf8_t>` to `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` line 18.

fine_trace.code: hb_blob_t *blob = hb_blob_create((const char *)data, size, HB_MEMORY_MODE_READONLY, NULL, NULL);
fine_trace.note: The harness forwards the raw PoC bytes into the library's blob constructor. This is the input-dependent call that reaches the first non-harness source step in `hb_blob_create()`.
First non-harness materialization of attacker input. The blob stores the fuzzer-controlled byte pointer that later backs `hb_face_create()` and `hb_font_create()` on the crashing shape path.
The first HarfBuzz buffer is populated with the fixed UTF-8 string `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`. MSan's allocation-origin stack ties the witnessed bug to this UTF-8 path, not to the later UTF-32 branch.
MSan allocation origin. Growing the fixed-text buffer's `info` array creates heap storage whose spare tail is left uninitialized until later writes touch specific glyph slots.
Appending text zero-initializes only the active entry at `info[len]` before filling its fields. The extra capacity from step 4 is not bulk-initialized, so slots beyond `len - 1` stay indeterminate.

This first `hb_shape()` call combines the attacker-controlled font created from step 2 with the fixed-text buffer prepared in step 3. The reproduced crash stack and reproduction report both correspond to this call site.
For horizontal shaping, feature collection always registers `kern` with fallback semantics in the planner map. This is planner-global state, not proof that the font itself exposes a `kern` feature.

depends_on.via: shape-plan construction for the first `hb_shape()` call

fine_trace.note: Compile materializes a non-zero `kern_mask` from the planner map built in step 7. On this path the mask is the planner's fallback kerning state, not a witness-specific font-derived property.
The non-zero planner mask from step 8 is converted to boolean `plan.has_kern = true`, satisfying the early return guard at the top of `_hb_ot_shape_fallback_kern()`.
The same face backed by step 2's blob is queried for GPOS. On the witnessed font this test is false, so `fallback_positioning` becomes true and `hb_ot_position()` later enters fallback kerning.
Before positioning, HarfBuzz initializes `mask` for the active glyph entries `info[0..len-1]`. The spare tail from step 4 is outside that range and remains untouched.

During `c->plan->substitute (c->font, buffer)`, `apply_string()` resets `buffer->idx = 0` at line 1227 and this forward GSUB walker runs until the cursor reaches `buffer->len`. On the witnessed path that end-of-loop state is the last pre-positioning value left in `buffer->idx`, and no later code before `hb_ot_position()` resets it.
Position clearing zeroes `pos` and resets output bookkeeping, but it never assigns to `idx`. The stale `buffer->idx == buffer->len` state from step 12 therefore survives into fallback positioning.

Root cause and MSan sink. The fallback-kern loop is indexed by local `idx`, but `buffer->cur()` dereferences `info[buffer->idx]`; with step 13 preserving `buffer->idx == buffer->len`, the guard reads `info[len].mask` from the uninitialized tail allocated in step 4 instead of the initialized in-range glyph at `info[idx]`. The patch fixes this by reading `info[idx].mask`.

format.name: OpenType font
format.contract: A font blob accepted by `hb_face_create()` and exercised through the harness's first UTF-8 `hb_shape(font, buffer, NULL, 0)` call. On the saved witness path, `!hb_ot_layout_has_positioning(face)` makes fallback positioning run, prior GSUB processing leaves `buffer->idx` stale at the end of the glyph buffer, and `_hb_ot_shape_fallback_kern()` tests `buffer->cur().mask` instead of `info[idx].mask`. With the fixed string `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`, the preserved `buffer->idx == buffer->len` causes the read of the first uninitialized tail slot in the buffer's `info` allocation. The saved evidence does not require the font itself to provide a `kern` feature; the non-zero `kern_mask` on this path is planner fallback state.
